## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical ability to implement per-tenant mTLS for CNF gateways using Kubernetes CSR flow and secret management without a global PKI.

## Key Concepts

- Kubernetes CertificateSigningRequest flow
- Per-namespace per-tenant CA
- Secret volumes and TLS configuration in a sidecar
- TLS handshake verification with control plane

## Code Example

```yaml
# CSR manifest (example)
apiVersion: certificates.k8s.io/v1
kind: CertificateSigningRequest
metadata:
  name: gateway-client-tenant-a
spec:
  groups:
  - system:authenticated
  request: <base64 CSR>
  usages:
  - digital signature
  - key encipherment
  - client auth
```

```yaml
# Secret CA manifest (example)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-ca
  namespace: tenant-a
type: Opaque
data:
  ca.crt: <base64-encoded CA cert>
```

```yaml
# Test manifest (gateway pod)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: gateway-test
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  containers:
  - name: gateway
    image: cnf/gateway:latest
    volumeMounts:
    - name: tls
      mountPath: /etc/certs
  volumes:
  - name: tls
    secret:
      secretName: tenant-a-gateway-client-cert
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you rotate per-tenant certificates without downtime?
- How would you validate client cert revocation in the control plane?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a per-tenant provenance flow, integrate image signing and SBOMs, and apply admission controls with policy-as-code. It also checks practical knowledge of Gatekeeper/OPA integration, namespace-scoped policies, and minimal test workflows.

## Key Concepts

- Cosign signing with tenant-specific keys
- SPDX SBOM attachment and verification
- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Per-tenant policy in a ConfigMap
- Minimal manifests and kubectl validation in a single namespace

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (yaml)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8simageprovenance
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sImageProvenance
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8simageprovenance
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Deployment"
        some c in input.review.object.spec.template.spec.containers
        not startswith(c.image, "ghcr.io/")
        msg := "image provenance missing or not tenant-approved"
      }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (yaml)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sImageProvenance
metadata:
  name: per-tenant-provenance
spec:
  enforcementAction: deny
  parameters:
    allowedTenant: "tenant-a"
```

```yaml
# Compliant Deployment (yaml)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: ghcr.io/tenant-a/gateway:v1.0.0
```

```yaml
# Noncompliant Deployment (yaml)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-gateway-bad
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: unsigned/gateway:latest
```

```bash
# Kubectl steps (one namespace first)
kubectl create ns tenant-a
# 1) Register constraint template and constraint
kubectl apply -f k8simageprovenance_template.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8simageprovenance_constraint.yaml
# 2) Sign and SBOM-attach a valid image (tenant-a key)
cosign sign --key cosign-tenant-a.key ghcr.io/tenant-a/gateway:v1.0.0
# 3) Deploy compliant manifest
kubectl apply -f compliant-deploy.yaml -n tenant-a
# 4) Deploy noncompliant manifest (unsigned)
kubectl apply -f noncompliant-deploy.yaml -n tenant-a
# 5) Check Gatekeeper denials and logs
kubectl get events -n tenant-a
kubectl describe deployment tenant-a-gateway-bad -n tenant-a
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you rotate tenant keys without downtime?
- How would you extend to multi-tenant namespaces concurrently?

```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: gateway-canary
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cnf-gateway
      tenant: tenant-a
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cnf-gateway
        tenant: tenant-a

      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: myregistry/cnf-gateway:canary
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080

      - setWeight: 10
      - pause: { duration: 1m }

```

- What metrics and alerting would you use to enforce the 0-downtime guarantee?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical knowledge of cross-tenant isolation using runtime attestation (SPIRE) and policy enforcement (OPA) in CNF meshes. It assesses understanding of real-world challenges including tenant scoping, short-lived credential management, and gateway security enforcement.

## Key Concepts
- SPIRE workload attestation and SVID binding to tenant ID
- OPA/Rego policy enforcement for tenant isolation
- Service mesh RBAC, namespaces, and tenant-scoped ServiceAccounts
- End-to-end testing within a single namespace

## Code Example
```yaml
# SPIRE Attestation
apiVersion: spire.spiffe.io/v1alpha1
kind: ClusterSPIFFEID
metadata:
  name: cnf-workload
spec:
  spiffeIDTemplate: "spiffe://example.com/ns/{namespace}/tenant/{tenant_id}"
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cnf
  tenantIDLabel: "tenant.id"
---
# OPA Authorization Policy
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-gateway-policy
  namespace: istio-system
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: istio-ingressgateway
  action: CUSTOM
  provider:
    name: opa
  rules:
  - when:
    - key: request.headers[x-spire-attestation]
      notValues: ["invalid"]
    - key: request.headers[x-tenant-capability]
      values: ["tenant-a-read", "tenant-a-write"]
---
# Test Manifest (single namespace)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: cnf-workload
  namespace: tenant-a
  labels:
    tenant.id: "tenant-a"
    tenant.capability: "read,write"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: cnf-api
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  selector:
    app: cnf
  ports:
  - port: 8080
    targetPort: 8080
```

## Why This Is Asked
Real-world upgrades in multi-tenant CNF platforms require safe, isolated releases. This tests your ability to design rollout strategies, implement metrics-based promotion decisions, and enforce cross-tenant risk controls.

## Key Concepts
- Argo Rollouts canary strategy scoped per tenant
- Tenant isolation via labels and service mesh subsets
- Per-tenant AnalysisRun with Prometheus-based SLAs
- Rollback and auto-promotion guardrails
- Minimal CRD sketches and namespace-scoped validation

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: gateway-rollout-tenant-a
  labels:
    tenant: a
spec:
  replicas: 3
  strategy:
    canary:
      steps:
        - setWeight: 10
        - analysis:
            templates:
              - templateName: tenant-a-analysis
        - setWeight: 30
        - analysis:
            templates:
              - templateName: tenant-a-analysis
        - setWeight: 100
      trafficRouting:
        nginx:
          stableIngress: gateway-ingress
          additionalIngressAnnotations:
            canary-by-header: X-Tenant-ID
      analysis:
        successfulRunHistoryLimit: 3
        unsuccessfulRunHistoryLimit: 3
```

## Per-Tenant AnalysisRun CRD Sketch
```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: AnalysisTemplate
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-analysis
spec:
  args:
    - name: tenant-id
  metrics:
    - name: latency-sli
      interval: 1m
      successCondition: result[0] <= 100
      failureLimit: 3
      provider:
        prometheus:
          address: http://prometheus:9090
          query: |-
            histogram_quantile(0.99,
              sum(rate(gateway_request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant="{{args.tenant-id}}"}[5m]))
              by (le))
    - name: error-rate-sli
      interval: 1m
      successCondition: result[0] <= 0.01
      failureLimit: 3
      provider:
        prometheus:
          address: http://prometheus:9090
          query: |-
            sum(rate(gateway_requests_total{tenant="{{args.tenant-id}},status=~"5.."}[5m]))
            /
            sum(rate(gateway_requests_total{tenant="{{args.tenant-id}}"}[5m]))
```

## One-Namespace Test Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-canary-test
  labels:
    tenant: a
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: gateway-stable
  namespace: tenant-a-canary-test
spec:
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
  selector:
    app: gateway
    role: stable
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: gateway-canary
  namespace: tenant-a-canary-test
spec:
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
  selector:
    app: gateway
    role: canary
---
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: gateway-rollout
  namespace: tenant-a-canary-test
  labels:
    tenant: a
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: gateway
          image: gateway:v2
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
  strategy:
    canary:
      canaryService: gateway-canary
      stableService: gateway-stable
      trafficRouting:
        service:
          canaryWeight: 10
      steps:
        - setWeight: 10
        - pause: {duration: 5m}
        - setWeight: 30
        - pause: {duration: 5m}
        - setWeight: 100
```

## Traffic Isolation Design
- **Service Mesh Subsets**: Each tenant gets dedicated subsets (stable/canary) in the mesh, ensuring zero cross-tenant traffic bleed
- **Tenant Labels**: All resources (Rollouts, Services, AnalysisRuns) are labeled with tenant ID for RBAC and policy enforcement
- **Network Policies**: Kubernetes NetworkPolicies restrict pod-to-pod communication to same-tenant pods only
- **Ingress Routing**: Use header-based routing (X-Tenant-ID) at the ingress to route to tenant-specific services

## Per-Tenant Metrics Collection
- Deploy tenant-scoped Prometheus instances or use Prometheus tenants
- Configure recording rules per tenant for SLI computation
- Metrics queries always include tenant filter to ensure isolation
- Store metrics with tenant label for multi-tenant querying and alerting

## Policy Enforcement
- **OPA/Gatekeeper**: Enforce that Rollouts must have tenant label and cannot modify other tenants' resources
- **Kubernetes RBAC**: Bind roles to tenant groups, limiting access to tenant-specific namespaces
- **Argo Rollouts RBAC**: Restrict Rollout/AnalysisTemplate access to tenant admins only

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to architect cross-cluster, tenant-isolated config rollouts with dynamic proxy configuration.

## Key Concepts
- Envoy xDS dynamic configuration and Aggregated Discovery Service (ADS)
- Kubernetes CRD-based policy model per tenant with isolation
- Canary traffic shaping with weight and time-based rollout window
- Multi-cluster consistency and safe rollback mechanisms
- Observability hooks for validation during rollout phases

## Code Example
```yaml
# (a) Tenant Routing Policy with Canary Weight and Rollout Window
apiVersion: cnf.example/v1
kind: TenantRoutePolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-api-v2
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  tenant: tenant-a
  targetCluster: cluster-west
  route:
    path: /api/v2
    backendRefs:
      - name: gateway-service
        port: 8080
  canary:
    weight: 0  # Start at 0%
    rolloutDuration: 30m
    stepWeight: 10  # Increment by 10% each step
    stepInterval: 5m
  rollback:
    enabled: true
    failureThreshold: 5  # Rollback if 5 consecutive errors exceed threshold
    errorRateThreshold: 0.05  # 5% error rate triggers rollback
  healthCheck:
    endpoint: /healthz
    interval: 30s
    timeout: 10s
---
# (b) Sidecar Config to Watch Policy and Push Updates
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: envoy-gateway-sidecar
  namespace: gateway-system
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: xds-controller
          image: cnf/xds-controller:latest
          args:
            - --policy-namespace=tenant-a
            - --xds-address=$(POD_IP):18000
            - --sync-interval=10s
          env:
            - name: POD_IP
              valueFrom:
                fieldRef:
                  fieldPath: status.podIP
          volumeMounts:
            - name: policy-config
              mountPath: /etc/policy
              readOnly: true
        - name: envoy
          image: envoyproxy/envoy:latest
          args:
            - --config-path /etc/envoy/envoy.yaml
            - --service-cluster gateway
          volumeMounts:
            - name: envoy-config
              mountPath: /etc/envoy
      volumes:
        - name: policy-config
          configMap:
            name: tenant-policies
        - name: envoy-config
          emptyDir: {}
---
# (c) One-Namespace Test Manifest for Canary Rollout and Rollback
apiVersion: cnf.example/v1
kind: CanaryRolloutTest
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-canary-test
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  policyRef:
    name: tenant-a-api-v2
  testStages:
    - stage: baseline
      duration: 5m
      expectedWeight: 0
      checks:
        - type: metrics
          metric: requests_total{path="/api/v2"}
          condition: equals 0
    - stage: canary_10pct
      duration: 10m
      expectedWeight: 10
      checks:
        - type: http
          url: http://gateway.tenanta.svc/health
          expectSuccessRate: 0.95
        - type: metrics
          metric: envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_xx{cluster="backend-v2"}
          condition: exists
    - stage: canary_50pct
      duration: 10m
      expectedWeight: 50
      checks:
        - type: http
          url: http://gateway.tenanta.svc/api/v2/users
          expectSuccessRate: 0.99
    - stage: full_rollout
      duration: 5m
      expectedWeight: 100
      checks:
        - type: http
          url: http://gateway.tenanta.svc/api/v2/**
          expectSuccessRate: 0.999
  rollbackTest:
    enabled: true
    triggerFailureAt: canary_50pct
    expectedBehavior: weight_reverts_to_0_within_2m
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical cache design in a CNF gateway, focusing on tenant isolation, hot-path optimization, and lifecycle of cached data.

## Key Concepts
- Cache-aside pattern with per-tenant keys

## Code Example
```go
package main

import (
  "time"
  "context"
  "github.com/go-redis/redis/v8"
)

type CacheClient struct{ Redis *redis.Client }

func (c *CacheClient) Get(ctx context.Context, tenant, path string) ([]byte, error) {
  key := tenant + ":" + path
  val, err := c.Redis.Get(ctx, key).Bytes()
  if err == nil {
    return val, nil
  }
  resp := fetchFromBackend(path) // placeholder
  c.Redis.Set(ctx, key, resp, 30*time.Second)
  return resp, nil
}
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical traffic shaping, per-tenant configuration, and end-to-end validation in CNF gateways. It favors deterministic routing to avoid flapping and shows how to wire a ConfigMap-driven control plane into a sidecar.

## Key Concepts
- Per-tenant canary rollout
- Deterministic routing via hashing
- Namespace-scoped ConfigMap as control plane

## Code Example
```javascript
function shouldCanary(tenantID, path, canaryEnabled, percent) {
  if (!canaryEnabled) return false;
  const h = hash(tenantID + path) // 32-bit
  return (h % 100) < percent;
}
```
